title: Roadblock Detection Fix Build Plan

approval: Build plan approved: roadblock detection fix

short.lead: I will build the fix in four steps under parent issue #587: better detection, a check of the failed-attempt record, two small-model checks, and a rule to never stop and wait in unattended or bypass mode. Please check the first card: three of the readings of your answers are my interpretation (the limit of 6 blocks, the end-of-turn timing with the mode gate, and where the goal comes from).
short.hint: Tap a step to see it.
items: Nine phrases that say I can't do something are always flagged. Four stall phrases ("not done", "I've stopped", "I've stopped here", "next step") are checked only at the end of a turn, and only in unattended or bypass mode. When one appears, a goal check decides whether I may stop. The goal check may block me up to 6 times in a row. A first try never counts as a failed attempt. A claim of "can't be done" must list three failed attempts that used different methods.
Tell me which reading is wrong, if any.

items.caption: My readings: the 6-block limit, the end-of-turn timing and the mode gate.

items: The claim check now matches both straight and curly apostrophes, ignores quoted lines, and adds the nine phrases and four stall phrases. It reads the permission mode, ignores system messages you did not write, and reads only the end of the transcript, not the whole file. It now blocks a retry exactly twice, then warns.

items.caption: Step 1 changes the claim pattern and the counter.

items: A claim that something can't be done passes only if the reply lists three failed attempts. They must use three kinds of method, such as a file check, a disk search and an attempt to run it. All three are aimed at the same target and can come from any tool. A reply that marks NEEDS YOU for a licence, login, purchase or destructive step is exempt.

items.caption: Three existence checks count as one kind.

items: A small model judges every reply at the end of a turn, looking for claims of inability that list fewer than three methods. When a stall phrase appears, a second check reads the session goal and decides whether work can carry on. Each model call costs about $0.002. If either check cannot run, it lets the reply through and says it could not run.

items.caption: Tested on three made-up sessions; the checks gave the right verdict in all three.

items: #590: never wait, plus docs, version and QA page

In unattended or bypass mode, when a design question comes up, I choose a reversible option and carry on. This adds one sentence to the rules and extends the hook that blocks questions so it also covers bypass mode. I also update the docs and version. After testing it myself, I post a QA page for you.
Nothing from you until the QA page.

items.caption: This rule applies only in unattended and bypass mode.

changes: scripts/house_rules/core.py: claim pattern, counter and turn window
Step 1 widens detection and fixes the block count.

Done when these new verify.py test cases pass. Each phrase is caught with both straight and curly apostrophes. A quoted claim is ignored. Stall phrases are scanned only in unattended or bypass mode. A retry is blocked a second time but never a third time.
Step 2 replaces the probe test with three related failed attempts.

Done when these cases pass. A claim made after only a git ls-files check is blocked. A claim made after three failed attempts that use three kinds of method, all named in the reply, is accepted. A failed PowerShell call or a failed tool call to another connected server counts as an attempt.
hooks/hooks.json and a nested goal check
Step 3 adds the judge hook and the goal check.

Done when these cases pass. A stall phrase with the goal reached passes. A stall phrase with the goal unreached blocks and gives the judge's reason. A missing or failing claude command-line program is announced and never blocks. The judge hook is listed in hooks.json.
show-dont-tell.md, the no-questions hook, docs and version
Step 4 stops me waiting for answers in unattended and bypass mode.

Done when these cases pass. An unattended session that ends with "next step" while its goal is unreached is blocked and carries on. A design question in bypass mode is denied, with the reason that I should choose and carry on. The injected rules stay under 9,700 characters when the plugin is installed at a path as long as the test runner's.
